questions.worked_solution:
To find the coordinates of the point, we inspect its position along the $x$- and $y$-axes.

* The point is $3$ units to the *right* of the origin, in the *positive* direction of the $x$-axis. So, its $x$-coordinate is $3.$

* The point is $2$ units *below* the origin, in the *negative* direction of the $y$-axis. So, its $y$-coordinate is $-2.$

Therefore, the coordinates of our point are $(3,-2).$

To find the length of $\overset{―}{AB},$ we use the distance formula:

questions.worked_solution:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

As we found previously, the slope is $m=-3.$

Substituting $m=-3$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y=-3x+b.
$$

We now need to find the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can find this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(3,-2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-3x+b \\ -2 & =-3(3)+b \\ -2 & =-9+b \\ 7 & =b \\ b & =7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=-3x+7.
$$

$$
y=-3x+7.
$$

At the $x$-intercept, the $y$-coordinate is equal to $0.$ So, we can substitute $y=0$ into the equation and then solve for $x:$

$$

questions.worked_solution:
Perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of each other. Therefore, since $\overset{↔}{AB}$ has the slope $m=-3,$ our perpendicular line must have a slope of 

$$
{m}_{1}=-\frac{1}{m}=-\frac{1}{(-3)}=\frac{1}{3}.
$$

So, our perpendicular line has the slope ${m}_{1}=\frac{1}{3}$ and passes through the point $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(3,-5).$ 

Finally, using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & ={m}_{1}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-5) & =\frac{1}{3}(x-3) \\ y+5 & =\frac{1}{3}x-1 \\ y & =\frac{1}{3}x-6\end{aligned}
$$
